```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "#>", collapse = TRUE)
library(CoRSIVtools)
pre <- readRDS("gse131433/gse131433_results.rds")
fig <- function(name) knitr::include_graphics(file.path("gse131433", "figures", paste0(name, ".png")))
show_df <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  num <- vapply(x, is.numeric, logical(1))
  x[num] <- lapply(x[num], signif, digits = digits)
  knitr::kable(x, row.names = FALSE)
}
n_fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
```

This vignette walks through a complete CoRSIV analysis of a public EPIC dataset,
**GSE131433**. The CHART cohort (Novakovic et al. 2019) profiled blood from
people conceived by assisted reproductive technology (ART) and from naturally
conceived controls. Each person was sampled twice: at birth from a Guthrie
(heel-prick) blood spot, and in adulthood from whole blood. We ask whether
methylation at CoRSIVs differs by mode of conception at each timepoint.

The input files are several GB, so the code below is shown but not run when the
vignette is built. Its outputs (tables and figures) were precomputed by two
scripts shipped with the package; the analysis was run on `r pre$run_date`.

```{r scripts, eval = FALSE}
system.file("scripts", "gse131433_prepare.R", package = "CoRSIVtools")   # GEO files -> annotated SE
system.file("scripts", "gse131433_analysis.R", package = "CoRSIVtools")  # SE -> results in this vignette
```

For a small example that runs in seconds, use `simulate_corsiv_data()`. It is
used in every function's help-page example.

# Data

## Inputs

CoRSIVtools needs three inputs:

- a normalised beta matrix (probes × samples);
- a sample metadata table;
- an hg38 probe manifest: a BED or Illumina CSV, or `"EPICv1"` / `"EPICv2"`.

From GEO we downloaded two files and never modified them:

- `GSE131433_series_matrix.txt`, the sample metadata;
- the supplementary `BorisNovakovicCHART_matrix_processed.csv`, with
  submitter-normalised (SWAN) betas and detection P values for
  `r n_fmt(pre$prepare$n_raw_probes)` probes in 440 arrays.

## Cleaning the GEO files

The series matrix stores metadata as tab-separated rows of `key: value`
strings. We parse it into one row per array, with these columns:

- `timepoint`, `conception` (reference level `natural`) and `sex`;
- the Sentrix `slide` and `position`, taken from the IDAT file names, plus
  `array_row`, the row part of the position.

```{r parse, eval = FALSE}
sm    <- readLines("GSE131433_series_matrix.txt")
field <- function(tag) lapply(grep(paste0("^!", tag, "\t"), sm, value = TRUE),
                              function(x) scan(text = x, what = "", sep = "\t", quiet = TRUE)[-1])
chars <- field("Sample_characteristics_ch1")            # "gender: F", "art status: ART", ...
ch    <- do.call(cbind, lapply(chars, function(v) sub("^[^:]+: ", "", v)))
colnames(ch) <- vapply(chars, function(v) unique(sub(":.*$", "", v)), "")
idat  <- field("Sample_supplementary_file")[[1]]        # .../GSM..._<slide>_<RxxCxx>_Grn.idat.gz
sx    <- regmatches(idat, regexec("_([0-9]+)_(R[0-9]+C[0-9]+)_Grn\\.idat", idat))
meta  <- data.frame(
  sample_id  = field("Sample_title")[[1]],               # matches the beta column names
  donor      = field("Sample_source_name_ch1")[[1]],
  timepoint  = factor(ifelse(ch[, "time of collection"] == "birth", "birth", "adult"), c("birth", "adult")),
  conception = factor(ifelse(ch[, "art status"] == "ART", "ART", "natural"), c("natural", "ART")),
  sex        = factor(ch[, "gender"], c("F", "M")),
  slide      = vapply(sx, `[`, "", 2),
  position   = vapply(sx, `[`, "", 3))
meta$array_row <- sub("C[0-9]+$", "", meta$position)
```

The processed CSV holds each sample's beta column next to its
`<sample>_Detection_Pval` column. The cleaning steps are:

1. Read both column sets.
2. Mask betas with detection P > 0.01.
3. Drop probes masked in more than 5% of samples
   (`r n_fmt(pre$prepare$n_probes_failed)` probes).
4. Keep `r n_fmt(pre$prepare$n_probes_kept)` probes.

The prepare script stops if the sample titles do not match the beta columns
one-to-one. It also stops if the timepoint or conception encoded in a title
disagrees with the characteristics fields.

```{r read, eval = FALSE}
dt    <- data.table::fread("BorisNovakovicCHART_matrix_processed.csv",
                           select = c("ID_REF", meta$sample_id, paste0(meta$sample_id, "_Detection_Pval")))
betas <- as.matrix(dt[, meta$sample_id, with = FALSE]); rownames(betas) <- dt$ID_REF
detp  <- as.matrix(dt[, paste0(meta$sample_id, "_Detection_Pval"), with = FALSE])
betas[detp > 0.01] <- NA
betas <- betas[rowMeans(detp > 0.01) <= 0.05, ]
```

## Building the SummarizedExperiment

`from_matrix()` checks that the betas and the metadata match one-to-one.
`annotate_probes()` attaches hg38 coordinates and averages replicate probes at
the same CpG.

```{r se, eval = FALSE}
se <- from_matrix(betas, meta, sample_col = "sample_id")
se <- annotate_probes(se, read_manifest("EPICv1"))   # needs IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICanno.ilm10b5.hg38
se
```

```{r se-out, echo = FALSE}
cat(pre$se, "\n")
```

```{r design-out, echo = FALSE}
show_df(stats::xtabs(Freq ~ timepoint + conception, pre$design_table))
```

# Quality control

We estimate blood cell fractions with EpiDISH, using the 7-cell-type
`centDHSbloodDMC` reference. `r pre$cells_meta$n_used` of its
`r pre$cells_meta$n_ref` reference CpGs are usable on this array. The
reference was built from adult blood and has no nucleated red blood cells, so
the newborn estimates are approximate. We then run the full QC suite. Slide and
array row are the technical variables.

```{r qc, eval = FALSE}
cells <- estimate_cell_fractions(se, ref = "centDHSbloodDMC")
for (cn in colnames(cells)) colData(se)[[cn]] <- cells[[cn]]
qc <- qc_report(se, vars = c("timepoint", "conception", "sex", "slide", "array_row"),
                technical = c("slide", "array_row"), cells = colnames(cells), group = "conception")
qc$summary
```

```{r qc-out, echo = FALSE}
show_df(pre$qc_summary)
```

## Samples

```{r qc-density, echo = FALSE, out.width = "85%"}
fig("qc_density")
```

The median sample is missing
`r signif(100 * pre$sample_missing$median_frac_missing, 2)`% of CpGs; the worst
is missing `r signif(100 * pre$sample_missing$max_frac_missing, 2)`%. `qc_samples()`
flags a sample on two rules: more than 5% of CpGs missing, or missingness more
than 3 MADs above the median. Here only the relative rule fires: it flags
`r pre$sample_missing$n_flag_relative` samples, mostly the dried blood spots,
which carry slightly more masked values than whole blood. The median is so
close to zero that "3 MADs above it" still means well under 3% missing, so no
samples were excluded. Inspect `qc$results$samples$table` before deciding on
exclusions in your own data.

## Batch and biology

PC1 explains `r round(100 * pre$qc_pca$var_explained[1])`% of the variance and
separates newborn blood spots from adult whole blood:

```{r qc-pca, echo = FALSE, out.width = "85%"}
fig("qc_pca_timepoint")
```

```{r qc-batch, echo = FALSE, out.width = "85%"}
fig("qc_batch")
```

The batch check is flagged because array row is associated with PC1. Most of
that is the timepoint: newborn and adult samples sit on different rows of the
chips. The more important question is whether a technical variable is
confounded with the *comparison* within each timepoint. Array row is:

```{r row-conf, eval = FALSE}
table(se$array_row[se$timepoint == "birth"], se$conception[se$timepoint == "birth"])
```

```{r row-conf-out, echo = FALSE}
pre$row_by_conception$birth
```

Most naturally conceived newborns sit on rows R05 to R07. Array row is
confounded with conception at both timepoints (simulated Fisher's exact
P < 10^-4^). Array position effects on Infinium chips are well documented, so
`array_row` goes into the model below. We first fitted the model without it.
24% (birth) and 37% (adulthood) of matched *background* regions then reached
P < 0.05 for ART, against 5% expected under the null. That pattern means a
technical artefact, not biology. With `array_row` in the model, the figure drops
to about 3%.

Cell composition does not differ by conception at either timepoint:

```{r qc-cells-out, echo = FALSE}
show_df(rbind(cbind(timepoint = "birth", pre$cells_by_timepoint$birth),
              cbind(timepoint = "adult", pre$cells_by_timepoint$adult)))
```

## CoRSIV biology checks

These two checks need no phenotype. They confirm that the probes map to the
right CoRSIVs and that the data carry real interindividual variation.

- The CoRSIVs at the two ends of *SPATC1L* should be anti-correlated.
- The *VTRNA2-1* CoRSIV should be bimodal.

Both pass. (They are also a sensitive test of genome build: with hg19 probe
coordinates, neither locus has any CpGs.)

```{r qc-loci, echo = FALSE, out.width = "48%", fig.show = "hold"}
fig("qc_spatc1l")
fig("qc_vtrna2")
```

# Target CoRSIVs and a matched background

`define_sets()` keeps CoRSIVs with at least 3 CpGs on the array. For each one,
it draws matched random control regions with the same width, probe count,
chromosome type and CpG density, 100 times. Sets depend only on array
coverage, so both timepoints share them. `summarise_regions()` averages the
CpGs in each region per sample.

```{r sets, eval = FALSE}
sets <- define_sets(se, background = "matched", n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
sets
coverage_report(sets)
reg  <- summarise_regions(se, sets)
```

```{r sets-out, echo = FALSE}
cat(pre$sets, "\n")
show_df(pre$coverage)
```

EPIC v1 reaches `r n_fmt(pre$coverage$n_ge1[1])` of the
`r n_fmt(pre$coverage$n_regions[1])` autosomal CoRSIVs, but only
`r pre$coverage$n_ge3[1]` have three or more CpGs. CoRSIVs are largely
invisible to standard arrays, which is why the coverage report matters. Per
draw, `r round(median(pre$match$n_matched))` targets (median) were matched.

# CoRSIV-level test, at birth and in adulthood

We fit `test_dm()` separately in each timepoint. It runs limma on the M-values
of the CoRSIV means, with the model below. Neutrophils and eosinophils are the
implicit reference among the cell fractions.

```{r test, eval = FALSE}
design <- ~ conception + sex + array_row + B + NK + CD4T + CD8T + Mono
res_birth <- test_dm(reg[, reg$timepoint == "birth"], design, coef = "conceptionART")
res_adult <- test_dm(reg[, reg$timepoint == "adult"], design, coef = "conceptionART")
```

```{r test-out, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
for (tp in c("birth", "adult")) {
  x <- pre[[tp]]
  cat(sprintf("\n**%s** (n = %d): %d of %d CoRSIVs at FDR < 0.05. Top 10:\n\n",
              tools::toTitleCase(tp), x$n, x$n_fdr, x$n_target))
  print(show_df(x$top))
}
```

```{r concord, echo = FALSE}
m <- merge(pre$birth$target, pre$adult$target, by = "region_id", suffixes = c("_birth", "_adult"))
r_db <- cor(m$delta_beta_birth, m$delta_beta_adult)
rk <- function(x, id) rank(x$P)[match(id, x$region_id)]
```

No CoRSIV passes FDR < 0.05 at birth. In adulthood,
`r pre$adult$n_fdr` do. Effects are small: the median |Δβ| across CoRSIVs is
`r signif(100 * pre$adult$distributions$target_abs_delta_beta[3], 2)` percentage
points in adulthood, and the largest is
`r round(100 * max(abs(pre$adult$target$delta_beta)), 1)` points. The ART
effect estimates agree well between timepoints (Pearson r = `r round(r_db, 2)`
for Δβ across all `r nrow(m)` CoRSIVs). chr6:27217501-27218800 ranks
`r rk(pre$birth$target, "chr6:27217501-27218800")` at birth and
`r rk(pre$adult$target, "chr6:27217501-27218800")` in adulthood;
chr14:105363801-105364800 ranks
`r rk(pre$birth$target, "chr14:105363801-105364800")` and
`r rk(pre$adult$target, "chr14:105363801-105364800")`. Newborns and adults are
largely the same people, so this agreement is not independent replication. It
does suggest a stable difference rather than noise.

```{r volcano, echo = FALSE, out.width = "48%", fig.show = "hold"}
fig("birth_volcano")
fig("adult_volcano")
```

```{r manhattan, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
fig("adult_manhattan")
```

`plot_corsiv()` shows the per-person data behind a result. Here is the top
CoRSIV in adulthood:

```{r top-corsiv, eval = FALSE}
plot_corsiv(reg[, reg$timepoint == "adult"], res_adult$region_id[which.min(res_adult$P)], "conception")
```

```{r top-corsiv-out, echo = FALSE, out.width = "55%"}
fig("adult_top_corsiv")
```

# Compare with the background

`compare_to_background()` asks two questions:

- Are CoRSIVs more often associated with ART than comparable random regions?
  This is the enrichment.
- Do CoRSIVs vary more between people? This is the variability.

```{r compare, eval = FALSE}
cmp_birth <- compare_to_background(res_birth)
cmp_adult <- compare_to_background(res_adult)
cmp_adult$enrichment
cmp_adult$variability
```

```{r compare-out, echo = FALSE}
enr <- rbind(cbind(timepoint = "birth", pre$birth$enrichment), cbind(timepoint = "adult", pre$adult$enrichment))
show_df(enr[, c("timepoint", "target_n", "target_frac_sig", "bg_mean_frac_sig", "empirical_p",
                "fisher_or", "target_n_fdr", "bg_mean_n_fdr")])
vb <- rbind(cbind(timepoint = "birth", pre$birth$variability), cbind(timepoint = "adult", pre$adult$variability))
show_df(vb)
```

Two background results stand out. First, at both timepoints CoRSIVs are about
three times more likely than matched control regions to reach P < 0.05 for ART:
`r round(100 * pre$birth$enrichment$target_frac_sig, 1)`% vs
`r round(100 * pre$birth$enrichment$bg_mean_frac_sig, 1)`% at birth, and
`r round(100 * pre$adult$enrichment$target_frac_sig, 1)`% vs
`r round(100 * pre$adult$enrichment$bg_mean_frac_sig, 1)`% in adulthood. No
background draw reached the CoRSIV fraction (empirical P =
`r signif(pre$adult$enrichment$empirical_p, 2)`, the minimum possible with 100
draws). Second, CoRSIVs are far more variable between people than matched
regions: median SD of beta `r signif(pre$adult$variability$target_median_sd, 2)`
vs `r signif(pre$adult$variability$bg_mean_median_sd, 2)` in adults. This is the
defining property of CoRSIVs, reproduced here in an independent cohort.

These results come from only `r pre$adult$n_target` CoRSIVs, with small effect
sizes. Treat them as hypothesis-generating. CoRSIV methylation is partly
genetically influenced, so a group difference there can also reflect genetic
or ancestry differences between the groups, not only the exposure. Matched
background regions do not control for this. Following up would need better
CoRSIV coverage than EPIC provides, for example targeted bisulfite sequencing.

```{r bg-plots, echo = FALSE, out.width = "48%", fig.show = "hold"}
fig("adult_bg_enrichment")
fig("adult_bg_variability")
```

# Exporting for bedtools

`write_bed()` writes standard 0-based BED files:

```{r bed, eval = FALSE}
write_bed(res_adult[res_adult$set == "target", ], "gse131433_adult_corsivs.bed")
```

# Caveats for this dataset

- Adult age is not in the GEO record, so it is not adjusted for.
- The ART group pools fresh-embryo, frozen-embryo and GIFT conceptions.
- Newborn and adult samples differ in tissue (dried blood spot vs whole blood)
  and were processed on different chip rows. Compare results across
  timepoints, not methylation levels.
- Most donors have arrays at both timepoints. A paired analysis
  (`design = ~ donor + timepoint`) is possible but not shown here.
